RefusalCode.description:
Why a file is not canonical.

The machine names are the `snake_case` of the variants, for example
`several_solids`. They never change meaning: a new check gets a new
code. The variants are in the order the checks run, which is the order
refusals are reported in.

fitment.features.description:
A features document: a part, or the reasons a file was refused.

A document comes only from [`read`](Self::read) or
[`from_json`](Self::from_json), and its fields are read through
methods, so every document this crate writes follows the rules
`from_json` checks. Its JSON keys are in a fixed order, every one is
written (absent values as `null`), and the same input gives the same
bytes on every operating system.

FitStatus.description:
Whether the candidate's body fits among the assembly's other solids.

Only [`FitStatus::Verified`] can make a [`Match`](crate::VerdictKind::Match),
and [`FitStatus::Interferes`] always makes a
[`Reject`](crate::VerdictKind::Reject). The other two leave an interface
that passed as an [`InterfaceMatch`](crate::VerdictKind::InterfaceMatch).

It serializes with a `status` tag, for example
`{"status":"not_checked","reason":"no fit verifier in this build"}`.
It is not deserializable: a fit result comes from a verifier, never from
a file.
